bullets.title: Friday's 5σ semi selloff was positioning unwind, not fundamental break
bullets.body: The NDX fell 4.8% and SOX fell 10% Friday—worst semi underperformance vs. S&P 500 in over 10 years. Drivers were multi-factor: AVGO earnings miss vs. elevated expectations, GOOGL's surprise $84.75B equity raise (stock -4%), META equity raise rumors (-6% for week), strong NFP report repricing Fed hike probability, and SpaceX IPO supply absorbing capital. Levered ETF flows amplified the move—SOXL traded $22B notional Friday. MS and others characterize it as a healthy correction from extreme positioning (SOX 75% above 200-DMA), not a fundamental deterioration. Monday futures are +0.7% with semis broadly up ~4%.

bullets.title: GOOGL's $84.75B equity raise signals 2027 capex heading toward $300B+
bullets.body: Alphabet upsized its raise to $84.75B ($18B stock + $16.75B mandatory convertible + $40B ATM + $10B Berkshire private placement) to fund AI infrastructure. Street consensus of ~$245B 2027 capex is seen as too low; buyside coalescing around $275-300B+. Bears note cost of equity (~4% yield) is cheaper than GOOGL's recent debt coupons (4.8%), making equity raise rational. Bulls model $16+ EPS in 2027 supporting $510 PT at 30x.

bullets.title: META equity raise speculation drove second leg of selloff; capex wave underway
bullets.body: FT reported META weighing tens of billions in new share sale to fund $145B AI capex, causing stock to drop 6-7% intraday. Multiple sources suggest META, MSFT, and AMZN could follow GOOGL, with aggregate Mag-7 capital raises potentially reaching $350-600B over the next 9-12 months. The debt channel is reportedly constrained for some hyperscalers, forcing expensive equity.

bullets.title: Goldman and GS push Fed cuts to 2027; futures pricing ~85% rate-hike probability
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs economist David Mericle now expects zero rate cuts in 2026, with the first cut pushed to 2027 given strong labor markets. May NFP came in at +172K with 93K upward revisions (3-month average 188K, highest since March 2024) and unemployment steady at 4.3%. Fed futures are pricing an 85% chance of at least one hike this year per Bianco/Hedgeye. The Strait of Hormuz supply shock—not labor—is the primary inflation wildcard, with Polymarket giving only 30% odds of normalization by end of July.

bullets.title: Iran-Israel escalation drives oil to $94, embeds inflation risk into yields
bullets.body: WTI spiked 4.6% to $94.40 (Brent +4% to $93+) after Israel struck Iran's Mahshahr petrochemical complex and Iran fired 10+ missiles at Israel. Iran is reportedly charging $1.5-2M per ship transiting Hormuz. JPM projects WTI at $95-97/bbl in Q2-Q3 assuming Strait remains open. The conflict is the primary driver of hawkish Fed sentiment and elevated 10-year yields. Trump said deal is 'very close' with two remaining sticking points, but Jefferies flags sequencing complexity.

bullets.title: Memory supply shortage to persist 'quite a few years'; cycle upgrades accelerating
bullets.body: Jensen Huang told audiences in South Korea that memory shortages will last several more years, driven by AI scaling demand. UBS raised DDR5 pricing forecasts to +67% QoQ in Q2 and +17% in Q3; NAND similarly upgraded. HBM blended ASPs forecast up 66% YoY in 2027 (HBM4E to $3.5/Gb). NVDA is cutting Vera Rubin SOCAMM2 from 1.5TB to 768GB due to supply constraints—but UBS models >2M Vera CPU units at 768GB as net neutral to demand. MS raised CY26 semi industry forecast from +91% to +103%.

bullets.title: S&P 500 snapped 9-week win streak; Monday rebounds +0.7% with tech leading
bullets.body: S&P 500 fell 2.6% Friday (NDX -4.8%, Russell 2000 -3.5%) in the worst breadth-on-a-down-day since 2000—advance/decline of just -21 on a >2% loss day. Mag-7 fell 5.3% equal-weight. VIX spiked above 20 for the first time in the quarter with QQQ put volume hitting all-time highs. S&P 500 futures are up +0.72% Monday morning as markets rebound; JPM maintains a cautious near-term view citing CPI/PPI risk (CPI Wednesday) and elevated equity issuance.

bullets.title: MRVL, FLEX join S&P 500 June 22; ROKU joins MidCap 400
bullets.body: Marvell Technology and Flex will replace Pool Corp and Campbell Soup in the S&P 500 effective June 22. Roku joins the S&P MidCap 400 before June 22 market open; stock up 3.9% in premarket. Jensen Huang reportedly called MRVL 'the next trillion dollar company.' MRVL stock rallied ~29% post-Computex and is +8.5% in Monday premarket.

bullets.title: AI capex economy increasingly supply-constrained; rolling shortages across entire physical layer
bullets.body: Multiple notes converge on one theme: the bottleneck is no longer demand or model quality but physical atoms—transformers, memory, CPUs, advanced packaging, networking, power components, and land. Hyperscalers have strong balance sheets and rising cloud receivables to fund multi-year buildouts. Raymond James silicon tour flagged supply chain constraints persisting through 2027-2028. Google secured 110K NVIDIA GPUs from SpaceX at $920M/month through mid-2029.

bullets.title: CPI Wednesday is the week's critical macro data point; hawkish print could drive 5% SPX pullback
bullets.body: JPM and 22V flag CPI as the key event risk. Current Core PCE at elevated levels increases odds of transitioning to a volatile regime with VIX above 20. Options are pricing a +/-90bp SPX move on June 10 CPI vs. 12-month average of +/-71bp. If inflation prints hot (0.3%+ monthly), JPM would turn bearish on hawkish data paired with ORCL/ADBE earnings risk. ORCL reports June 10, ADBE June 11, RH June 11.

bullets.title: NVDA-SK Hynix partnership deepens; CEO calls tech selloff a 'buying opportunity'
bullets.body: NVIDIA announced a multi-year partnership with SK Hynix covering next-gen AI memory including HBM4 for Vera CPUs, RTX Spark, and Jetson platforms. SK Hynix plans to nearly double DRAM wafer production from 550K to ~1M wpm by 2030-2031. Jensen Huang publicly called the global tech selloff a 'buying opportunity,' and answered 'yes' when asked whether it's time to buy NVDA stock. NVDA is also doubling H2 supply chain capacity.

bullets.title: Macro: Strong U.S. economy with 3% GDP forecast, broadening capex, improving LFPR
bullets.body: Nancy Lazar (macro) flags prime-age LFPR back near all-time highs, ISM Manufacturing at 54.0 (highest since May 2022), and non-tech capex cycle broadening to factory construction. S&P 500 EPS expected +21.7% YoY in Q2. Fed's 175bp of cuts have lagged impact supporting employment. Housing affordability improving with new home prices -9% from peak. 3% GDP forecast for 2026 driven by lagged Fed easing, capex expensing, AI productivity, and good employment breadth.

bullets.title: JPM tactically cautious: prefers Energy, Financials, Healthcare; short broader Tech
bullets.body: JPM's market intelligence team recommends a defensive stance until CPI prints and bond volatility dissipates. They favor long Energy (WTI $95/Q2), Financials, and Healthcare vs. short Unprofitable Tech and broader Tech. Mag-7 is recommended as a safety haven but paired with shorts in ex-Mag-7 tech. Factor unwinds (Momentum/Beta) present near-term risk. APAC markets are down sharply (Korea -8%, circuit breaker triggered; NKY -4.2%; HSI -1.4%). A US-Iran deal would be the signal for an 'everything rally.'

bullets.title: Semis still 'the new oil' but extended; UBS overweight on fundamentals, supply constraints
bullets.body: UBS argues semis are now 12% of global market cap (up from 2.7% in 2022) and could reach 2-3% of global GDP by 2030 ($3T TAM). P/E at 37x vs. 45-72x in prior bubbles. Hyperscaler capex in 2027 must rise 33% from 2026 to exceed free cash flow, and memory capex could reach 57% of hyperscaler spending by 2027. UBS top buys: TSMC, MU, SK Hynix. SOX had 77% rally in two months—precedent historically is one good signal and one sell signal.

bullets.title: USMCA review, US trade policy shifting to discretionary/sectoral regime
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags US trade policy transitioning from rules-based to discretionary, sector-specific industrial policy. Canada's manufacturing export base (autos, metals) is most exposed; Mexico benefits from nearshoring. AI-linked imports (electronics, semis, data infrastructure) are the fastest-growing category. Morgan Stanley expects tariff-driven goods inflation to give back in 2H26, supporting Fed easing into 2027. MS is hosting a USMCA webcast today at 10am.

bullets.title: AAPL WWDC today: Gemini-based Siri with agentic capabilities; stock historically +11% June-Sept
bullets.body: Apple's WWDC keynote at 1pm ET features redesigned Siri with on-screen awareness and personal context powered by Gemini integration. iPhone 18 base models are not until C1Q27; fall is the Pro/Foldable story. JPM notes AAPL models ~$50 price increases on iPhone 18 to protect margins against memory cost headwinds. JPM expects AAPL to outperform SPX ~11% June to mid-September into fall launches. KeyBanc maintains Sector Weight, citing 24x FY27 EV/EBITDA as overvalued.

bullets.title: Cerebras Systems: Multiple Buy initiations on fast-inference leadership
bullets.body: Citi ($340 PT, Buy), UBS ($300 PT, Buy), and Morgan Stanley ($250 PT, OW) all initiated coverage of Cerebras (CBRS), highlighting its wafer-scale architecture 2-3x faster than NVIDIA GB200 on token throughput. Key: Cerebras is the only supplier currently shipping to OpenAI (70%+ revenue concentration through 2028) and is growing with AWS. Fast inference TAM projects from $113B (2025) to $649B (2030) at 42% CAGR. Primary risk is NVIDIA competition and supply chain scaling.

bullets.title: 2-year Treasury yield targeting 5%; parabolic semi stocks face sustained correction risk
bullets.body: Technicians flag the 2-year yield breaking to new reaction highs with a target of 5%. SNDK was 250% above its 200-DMA, MRVL 220%, MU 200%, and DELL 195% above their respective 200-DMAs prior to Friday. The Philadelphia Semi Index peaked at 76% above its 200-DMA (>3 standard deviations). Gold and silver are vulnerable; Bitcoin retested $60K downside with risk to $40K per some technicians.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO oversubscribed 2x; equity supply wave absorbing tech market liquidity
bullets.body: SpaceX's $75B IPO is reportedly 2x oversubscribed (~$150B demand) with pricing expected this week (Friday June 12). Retail minimum dropped to $2K. Polymarket gives 64% odds SpaceX opens above a $2T valuation. The IPO, combined with GOOGL's equity raise and META's potential offer, is seen as a supply-driven headwind for tech equities. Jefferies noted that systematic fund rebalancing tied to mega-cap equity issuance was a key driver of Friday's selloff.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley bullish: 'healthy reset,' maintains S&P 500 year-end target of 8,000
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley characterizes Friday's selloff as a healthy correction enabling bull market extension. Earnings revisions breadth for S&P 500 is at 26%, a new cycle high. ISM Manufacturing at 54 and average private payroll gains of 166K (strongest since 2023) underpin the bull case. Next leadership expected in Consumer Discretionary, Transports, and Regional Banks. MS also notes no rate hike risk premium is justified given disinflationary wage dynamics (AHE 3.4% YoY) and expects lower 10-year yields on forecast horizon.
